title: FlowSearcher: Synthesizing Memory-Guided Agentic Workflows for Web Information Seeking
claim: A two-level agent synthesizes task-adaptive workflow graphs, guided by a hierarchical memory of past traces reused across queries.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right; rounded containers; central orchestrator flow with memory column
description: A wide figure with three rounded containers. The left panel, 'Workflow Synthesis', shows tool-use patterns (General, Parallel, Swift-Hit, Break-Down) as small node-and-arrow graphs. Below them, three dashed boxes (Web Navigation, Quick Look-up, Surveying) show workflows built from colored blocks: orange for Search, blue for Browse, green for Summarize. The middle panel, 'Two-level Trajectory', has a high-level chain of sub-goal circles above a dashed line. Under the line, a robot icon labeled Orchestrator receives numbered steps: (1) experience injection from a speech-bubble hint, then (2) memory-guided workflow synthesis. This feeds a dashed execution box with a parallel node graph and an 'Inject' arrow. The right peach panel, 'Hierarchical Memory', stacks task-level, graph-level and node-level records, each with small icons and example text. The eye goes first to the robot and the left-panel graphs.
caption: An overview of the FlowSearcher framework. Left: FlowSearcher synthesizes diverse tool-use patterns into task-adaptive workflow graphs, enabling different strategies for navigation, look-up, and surveying. Middle: A two-level search trajectory separates high-level orchestration from low-level execution: the orchestrator decomposes the query into sub-goals and synthesizes workflows conditioned on retrieved experience, while the executor performs memory-guided workflow execution. Right: A hierarchical memory records execution traces at the task, graph, and node levels, which are retrieved to guide both workflow synthesis and execution, enabling experiencedriven reuse and adaptation across queries.
abstract: Web search is a cornerstone for deep research agents, enabling them to acquire and reason over knowledge beyond static corpora. Yet most existing systems rely on ReAct-style tool chains with rigid, linear workflows, hindering their ability to adapt to diverse query types and tool-use strategies. We introduce FlowSearcher , a novel deep search framework that formulates web information seeking as memory-guided agentic workflow synthesis . FlowSearcher decomposes a query into subgoals and synthesizes a tailored workflow graph for each subgoal, dynamically adapting the depth, ordering, and composition of tool use. Complementing this, a hierarchical memory consolidates past workflows into reusable structural experience, which is retrieved to guide both workflow orchestration and execution on new queries. By shifting from reactive tool calls to experience-conditioned workflow design, FlowSearcher enables flexible multi-path exploration and reuse without any supervised training or RLHF. Experiments on GAIA, BrowseComp, and GPQA show that FlowSearcher consistently matches or exceeds the performance of RLHF-trained web agents under the same model backbone. Our code is released at github.com/XiangKeYiNTU/flowsearcher .
